page: Microsoft Azure L2as_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 2 dedicated vCPUs based on AMD x86_64 processor architecture alongside 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Accelerated GPU processing is absent from this configuration, concentrating system resources strictly on compute, memory, and high-throughput local disk storage.

A central component of the L2as_v5 profile is its integrated local storage, which includes a 480 GB NVMe SSD. In addition to direct NVMe disk access, the instance is capable of attaching Premium Storage tiers for external persistent workloads. With an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio and direct NVMe storage, the architecture targets operations that require low disk latency paired with moderate memory residency.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides high-speed local NVMe storage and dedicated execution cores without requiring oversized virtual machine allocations. Tradeoffs center on the dual-core compute footprint and the absence of bundled public IPv4 routing, making it best matched to targeted backend storage components rather than compute-bound processing or distributed parallel execution.

Azure L2as_v5 fits low-footprint transactional databases, intermediate caching tiers, NoSQL nodes, search engine indexes, and logging agents requiring fast local scratch storage and reliable read-write speeds.
